verdict.rationale: Snowflake's own SQL reference documents native window functions and first-class semi-structured types (VARIANT/OBJECT/ARRAY) for JSON and arrays, with no extensions needed. A community commenter's hands-on use of windowing-function queries corroborates the window-function part. Missing for 10: any evidence of CTE support, any evidence of rich date/time types, and independent corroboration of the semi-structured/array querying.

support.subject: As an analyst, I get a full analytical SQL surface — window functions, CTEs, semi-structured JSON, arrays, and rich date/time types — without bolt-on extensions

citations.quote: Window functions are analytic functions that you can use for various calculations such as running totals, moving averages, and rankings
JSON and arrays are first-class SQL types.
They modified windowing-function approaches and found the approach "several OOM faster because of partition elimination."
